\chapter{Boolean Analysis — Basic}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.Randomization.Basic
\section{Overview}
Orthogonal projections, conditional expectation, and product noise satisfy finite spectral identities. Weighted moment contraction and energy decompositions provide approximation criteria for Boolean juntas.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{theorem}[Signed intersection cancellation]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.RandomizationAux.signed_intersection_zero}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
Let $S$ and $J$ be finite subsets of a set, and let $g$ be a real-valued function on its
finite subsets. If $S\nsubseteq J$, then $\sum_{T\subseteq S}(-1)^{|S|-|T|}g(T\cap
J)=0$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Conditional expectation of a component]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.RandomizationAux.condExp_component}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.Point, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.component, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.condExp, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.condExp_comp, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.expect, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.expect_sum_mul, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.RandomizationAux.signed_intersection_zero}
\difficulty{5}
Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom
masses, let $J$ and $S$ be sets of coordinates, let $f$ be a real-valued function on the
product space, and let $x$ be an outcome. The conditional expectation over coordinates
outside $J$ of the $S$-component of $f$, evaluated at $x$, equals that component at $x$
if $S\subseteq J$, and equals zero otherwise.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Signed subset inversion identity]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.RandomizationAux.sum_powerset_signed_sum}
\leanok
\difficulty{5}
Let $U$ be a finite subset of a type with decidable equality, and let $g$ be a
real-valued function on its finite subsets. Then $\sum_{S\subseteq U}\sum_{T\subseteq
S}(-1)^{|S|-|T|}g(T)=g(U)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Weighted absolute-power inequality]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.RandomizationAux.weighted_abs_rpow_sum_le}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
Let $s$ be a finite set, let $w,F:s\to\mathbb R$, and suppose $w(a)\ge0$ for every $a\in
s$, $\sum_{a\in s}w(a)=1$, and $q\ge1$. Then $\left|\sum_{a\in
s}w(a)F(a)\right|^q\le\sum_{a\in s}w(a)|F(a)|^q$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Weighted negative moment inequality]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.RandomizationAux.weighted_negative_moment_le}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.CenteredContraction.scalar_affine}
\difficulty{4}
Let $\alpha$ be a type, let $s$ be a finite subset of $\alpha$, and let $w,F:s\to\mathbb
R$ be given, with $w_i\ge0$ for every $i\in s$ and $\sum_{i\in s}w_i=1$. Suppose $q>0$,
$0\le c\le1$, and for every $z\in\mathbb R$, $|1-cz|^q\le |1+z|^q-q(1+c)z$. Set
$a=\sum_{i\in s}w_iF_i$. Then $\sum_{i\in s}w_i|a-c(F_i-a)|^q\le\sum_{i\in
s}w_i|F_i|^q$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Conditional reflected-moment contraction]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.RandomizationAux.condExp_negative_moment_le}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.Point, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.condExp, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.expect, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.expect_const, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.expect_swap_samples, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.mass, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.mass_sum, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.RandomizationAux.weighted_negative_moment_le}
\difficulty{5}
Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom
masses, let $J$ be a set of coordinates, let $f$ be a real-valued function on the
product space, and let $q,c\in\mathbb R$ satisfy $0<q$ and $0\le c\le1$. Suppose that
$|1-cz|^q\le |1+z|^q-q(1+c)z$ for every real $z$. Then the product expectation of
$|E_Jf-c(f-E_Jf)|^q$ is at most the product expectation of $|f|^q$, where $E_J$ denotes
conditional expectation over coordinates outside $J$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Boolean junta approximation from energy bounds]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.RandomizationAux.exists_boolean_junta_of_energy_bounds}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.DependsOn, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.IsBoolean, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.Point, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.component, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.condExp, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.exists_boolean_rounding, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.expect, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.prob, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.RandomizationAux.condExp_residual_secondMoment}
\difficulty{5}
Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom
masses, and let $f$ take values in $\{-1,1\}$ on its outcome space. For a coordinate set
$J\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, an integer $k\ge 0$, and real numbers $a,b$, suppose the
total expected squared component energy over sets $S$ with $|S|>k$ is at most $a$, and
the corresponding total over sets with $|S|\le k$ but $S\nsubseteq J$ is at most $b$.
Then there is a function $g$ taking values in $\{-1,1\}$, depending only on coordinates
in $J$, such that $\Pr_P(f\ne g)\le a+b$.
\end{theorem}
